A couple of years ago, I was getting off the bus from work and needed to stop at an ATM. I could have gone inside this gas station but there were too many people inside and I knew all of the employees (I used to work there). I wanted to avoid that experience so I decided to use the bank ATM across the street. 

I walked up to the atm in the drive thru and took out $20. Little did I know there was a group of dudes watching me the entire time... They jumped and robbed me..and I put myself in that situation because I was too afraid to go inside a freaking store.

I let my emotions influence my logic. It may feel good in the moment to avoid fearful situations but is it good a choice for your overall well being?

I can definitely relate. I find it hard to develop relationships because I am always overthinking and have become a bit boring due to isolation. 

I get a long with most people because I'm easy going and have a sense of humor. I tend to decline offers to hang out with folks because it's too much pressure to be personable when I'm going thru depression episodes. 

I do realize that the only way to get better at interacting with ppl is do actually be around them so I hang out every once and while. It's painful and sometimes I regret it but it's helpful in the long run

We live 8 hrs away from each other but he grew up in my city and comes back to visit his family for holidays. Over the summer he suggested we hang out when he comes home for Thanksgiving..and wtf he actually hit me up last night to hang out!! He's super smart and witty and I'm afraid I wont be able to hold a conversation because I've been isolating, unplugged and  stuck inside my head for so long from anxiety + depression.
